chunks: And Hammad reported from Ibrahim ibn Abi Yahya, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
And the dirhams at that time weighed six (units).
ai.seo_question: What was the weight of a dirham in the time of the Imams?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), transmitted via Hammad ibn Uthman, establishes the specific weight standard of the dirham during the early Islamic period, providing crucial historical data for fiqh al-mu'amalat. It highlights the precision required in measuring currency for valid dowries (mahr) and commercial transactions, reflecting the Shia emphasis on adhering to established economic norms of the Ahl al-Bayt's time. This context aids jurists in determining the minimum value (nisab) and fairness in financial obligations.

en.hubeali:
And Hammad reported from Ibrahim Bin Abu Yahya, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘And the Dirham in those days used to be the weight of six (Dirhams today)’.
en.sarwar: 6. And Hammad has narrated from Ibrahim ibn abu Yahya who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
The weight of dirham in those days was six.’”
